newsitem.title: USA: US Mid-Atlantic spot power slips ahead of holiday.
newsitem.headline: US Mid-Atlantic spot power slips ahead of holiday.

text.p: Spot prices of wholesale electricity in the Mid-Atlantic U.S. slipped Wednesday amid softer natural gas prices ahead of the Thanksgiving holiday weekend.
"There should be enough weather-related load to compensate for lower baseload demand," a Mid-Atlantic trader said, referring to load projection for the region on Thanksgiving.
Thursday, temperatures in the midsection of the Atlantic season were predicted to peak in 30s Fahrenheit and bottom in the 20s, which would be eight to 14 degrees below normal.
Extended outlook showed temperatures would moderate over the weekend.
NYMEX January 1997 Henry Hub natural gas futures closed down 9.6 cents at $3.485 per million British thermal units.
With marketers and most Pennsylvania-New Jersey-Maryland (PJM) Interconnect utilities closing Thursday and Friday, daily power schedulings were completed through Monday, brokers and marketers said.
Firm, peak PJM electricity for Thursday was quoted at $22.00-$23.00 a megawatt hour (MWh), Friday $23.50-$24.50, Saturday $20.00-$20.25, Sunday $18.75-$19.25 and Monday $26.25-$27.00.
Today's firm, peak next-day quotes compared with Tuesday's $25.25-$26.25 for Wednesday.
Firm, off-peak PJM electricity for Thursday was valued near $16.00, Friday $15.00-$16.00, Saturday and Sunday $12.00-$16.00, and Monday $13.00-!6.50.
Those daily firm, off-peak assessements compared with Tuesday's $17.25 for Wednesday.
December PJM power was valued at $27.50-$28.00, down from Tuesday's $28.75-$28.95.
January/February 1997 PJM electricity was assessed at $32.80-$33.10, off from $33.35-$33.65 Tuesday.
March 1997 PJM deliveries were talked at $25.50-$25.75, a tighter range than Tuesday's $25.50-$26.40.
Second-quarter 1997 PJM deliveries were discussed at $22.80-$22.90, slightly stronger bid than $22.75-$22.90 Tuesday.
July/August 1997 PJM power was quoted at $32.00-$32.35, compared with quote of $32.05 Tuesday.
A 600 megawatt (MW) unit at the coal-fired Homer City, Pa., generating station was planned to resume service today after being shut Monday for repairs.
